I'll take this. The fix is to extend `TuiPluginApi.state` (packages/plugin/src/tui.ts) so a status-line plugin can read the live selected model/agent that the prompt input actually has on screen. The current gap is that `state.session.get(id).model` only mirrors the server-side value (set on the next `session.prompt`), and the in-memory selection lives in the private Solid store at `packages/tui/src/context/local.tsx`. The save() side already persists `recent` / `favorite` / `variant` to model.json — adding the active selection to that same payload keeps it consistent.

Plan: thread the active selection through the Solid `Local` store, surface it as a reactive read on the plugin state, and persist it alongside the recent/favorite set so refreshes can rebuild it. Cover with a TUI test that flips the model via the prompt and asserts the plugin sees the new value before the next prompt is sent.

Fixes #50315

Fixed in #50383 (merged as ddeb19790a). `reasoning_details` is now decoded against the known OpenRouter and Kimi shapes at the boundary; Kimi `summary` / `encrypted` entries are replayed without the stream-only `index` and alongside `reasoning_content`, so the follow-up request after tool calls no longer 400s.

Thanks for the pointers. The plugin half of this report duplicates #49389 (item 1) and #47229, so I'll follow those for `session.compact` on the plugin context.

I'm narrowing this issue to the part none of them covers: compaction after **idle time**. #40113 asks for a size-based threshold, which v2 already has as `compaction.auto`. This one is about compacting a large session before its prompt cache expires, so the first message after a long break doesn't re-send the whole context uncached. Retitled to match.

Another use case for item 1 (`session.compact`): a server plugin that keeps idle sessions' prompt caches warm wants to compact the session when its idle window ends, so the first message after a long break doesn't re-send the whole context uncached. It can detect the end of the window but has no way to start the compaction. Idle-time compaction in core is tracked separately in #50777; exposing `compact` here would let a plugin cover it.

Field report from an agent that used this tool on Windows 11 / desktop 2.0.14 — full measurements in #50781.

In short: `screenshot` refuses with "needs a visible tab" whenever the tab's view is not composited (the review pane is displaying another session), while `snapshot` / `evaluate` / `navigate` keep working on the same tab. Window focus, tab focus and pane instantiation were each tested and are not the cause; the hidden `Chrome_WidgetWin_0` hosting the view is.

The `fromSurface: true` call is what cannot succeed in that state. A fallback to `fromSurface: false` (with `captureBeyondViewport: false`) makes capture work there and leaves the visible case untouched — sketch in the issue.

Also worth knowing: `click` / `type` already go through `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` / `Input.insertText`, which do not need a surface, so the `UnknownVizError` I saw on `click` is likely a host-side visibility gate rather than something this file can fix.

Happy to re-test against a build that includes the fallback.

The browser tool landing in #48755 still cannot capture while the review pane is not displaying the tab: `screenshot` requires a composited surface (`fromSurface: true`) and refuses with "needs a visible tab", while the DOM actions keep working.

Filed with measurements, the exact precondition, and a suggested `fromSurface: false` fallback: #50781

## Additional technical detail (root cause analysis)

Confirming and extending #50650 from the **`opencode serve` / web-UI** side (not just Desktop).
Environment: `opencode` 2.0.12, `opencode serve` + browser UI. Same unconditional throw.

### 1. The stub is not protocol-independent in `dev`

On the 2.0.12 release the handler is untouched:

```js
// packages/app/src/providers/credentials/dialog.tsx
mutationFn: async (result) => {
  // TODO: Restore custom providers when V2 exposes config and arbitrary credential APIs.
  throw new Error(language.t("provider.custom.unavailable"))
}
```

On `dev` it has been partially implemented, but is gated behind a **v1-only** server check
(`packages/app/src/components/dialog-custom-provider.tsx:134`):

```ts
if ((await serverSDK().protocol) !== "v1") throw new Error(language.t("provider.custom.unavailable"))
```

And `packages/app/src/utils/server-protocol.ts` probes for the legacy endpoint:

```ts
const legacy = await probe(server, fetch, "/global/health").catch(() => undefined)
if (legacy && "healthy" in legacy && legacy.healthy === true) return "v1"
```

**So the dialog can only ever work against a v1 server.** That is consistent with the TODO, but it
means the feature is not merely "not implemented yet" — it is actively gated off for v2 servers.

### 2. The write APIs genuinely do not exist on a v2 server (verified)

I enumerated every registered route in `packages/server/src/handlers/` for 2.0.12:
**all of them are `.get()`**, except one `.put()` on a session handler. There is no config write,
and no `auth.set`.

Probing a live `opencode serve` 2.0.12 instance:

```
POST   /api/config    -> 404      PUT /api/config    -> 404
POST   /api/auth      -> 404      PUT /api/auth      -> 404
POST   /api/provider  -> 404      PUT /api/provider  -> 404
```

So the `TODO` comment is accurate — there is no client-side workaround. This matches the
reporter of #50650 observing that the app's own source references a `serverSDK().client.auth.set(...)`
that has no counterpart on the server.

### 3. There is also no `opencode config` write command as a fallback

`opencode config` only exposes `list` / `path`. `opencode config set …` falls through to the default
handler and just launches the TUI. So neither the UI nor the CLI can persist a custom provider.

### 4. Workaround that does work

Hand-editing the global config is unaffected — the engine loads it correctly on the same server
where the dialog throws. Two substitutions are supported (`packages/core/src/config/variable.ts`):

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json   (XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/opencode.json)
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "deepseek": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "DeepSeek",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "https://api.deepseek.com/v1",
        "apiKey": "{env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}"
      },
      "models": { "deepseek-chat": { "name": "DeepSeek Chat" } }
    }
  }
}
```

`{env:VAR}` reads from the process env, `{file:path}` from a file (supports `~/`) — both are useful
for keeping the key out of the config file.

This is what the reporter meant by "works when added manually" — but it is worth stating explicitly
that this is the **only** path today, because the protocol gate in `dev` means even a future v2
implementation must add the missing server endpoints first.

### Suggested split

- **Server**: add config write + credential write endpoints (`/api/config`, `/api/auth`).
- **App**: then the existing `dev` implementation can drop the `!== "v1"` gate.

Until the server side exists, the UI should probably hide the custom-provider entry rather than
present a form that cannot be submitted — showing it implies the feature is available.

Adding a macOS (darwin-arm64) data point for the same root cause, plus a second cost that this leak causes on macOS.

**Version:** opencode-ai 1.18.25; `BUN_BE_BUN=1 opencode --version` → `1.3.14`. The v1 `dev` branch `package.json` still has `"packageManager": "bun@1.3.14"`.

**Same shape on macOS, and it isn't only libopentui.** Each `opencode serve` / `attach` / TUI launch writes its embedded native libraries under a new random name and never removes the dylibs. For example, the fff `c-lib`:

| launch | file | inode |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `$TMPDIR/.b9dff6ede3bff3ba-00000000.dylib` (4,822,976 B) | 477118107 |
| 2 | `$TMPDIR/.b9dff6edfefebfa2-00000000.dylib` (same bytes) | 477118129 |
| 3 | `$TMPDIR/.b9dff6eff3fe37ca-00000000.dylib` (same bytes) | 477118144 |

`libopentui.dylib` (3.3–3.8 MB) behaves the same way for the TUI. One long-running macOS host we use for testing had built up 22,984 of these files, 43.3 GB in total.

**Second cost, specific to macOS: slow first `dlopen`.** Because every launch writes a new inode, macOS runs its first-load Gatekeeper assessment on the library every time. `dlopen` blocks the main thread in `fcntl` while `syspolicyd` evaluates the file. That's 0.2–0.8 s per library on an idle Mac. On a busy host it was 92–114 s, because `syspolicyd` processes the assessments one at a time and the leaked files keep adding to that queue. Re-opening the same file takes 0.00 s. So on macOS the leak also slows down every cold start, not just the disk.

`BUN_TMPDIR` / `TMPDIR` move the files elsewhere, but the names still change on every launch.

**Ask:** build the 1.18.x releases with Bun ≥ 1.4.0 (oven-sh/bun#29587: content-hash names, reused across launches), or backport that change. That fixes both the leak and the per-launch assessment cost. #39876 was closed as fixed in V2 only.

**Repro (macOS)**
```sh
for i in 1 2 3; do opencode serve --port 0 & P=$!; sleep 5; lsof -p $P | grep "$TMPDIR" | grep -E '\.(dylib|node)$'; kill $P; wait $P 2>/dev/null; done
ls -A "$TMPDIR" | grep -cE '^\.[0-9a-f]{16}-[0-9]{8}\.dylib$'   # grows on every launch
```

Another headless data point, and a mechanism I don't think is in this thread yet: whether a `length` finish ends the run depends on the auto-compaction threshold, which makes it fatal precisely when there is context to spare.

Terminal-Bench 4.0, OpenCode 1.18.31, OpenAI-compatible local provider, model limit `context: 131072, output: 65536`, effective cap 32,000 (#29363). Five truncations across three trials:

| context at truncation | >= usable | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 42,975 | no | run ended |
| 48,595 | no | run ended |
| 99,918 | yes | continued |
| 124,651 | yes | continued |
| 66,729 | no | run ended |

`usable = 131,072 - min(65,536, 32,000) = 99,072`, so the threshold predicts all five.

The two that continued did so because `compaction.isOverflow` fired on the preceding step. The compaction inserts a new user message, so the `lastAssistant.parentID === lastUser.id` clause at `prompt.ts:1115` no longer holds and the exit at `:1113` is skipped. Nothing branches on `length`, as #40146 notes, so the rescue is incidental rather than intended.

This also qualifies the point above that raising the limit only postpones the failure. Here it also lowers the compaction threshold, since usable is context minus the cap. Raising the cap to 65,536 would move the threshold from 99,072 to 65,536, so truncations that still occur would be more likely to compact and continue instead of ending the run.

Cost in this run: three of eight scored trials ended this way, one of them after 6.9 hours of work, all recorded with no error.

The numbers behind this report:

| | |
|---|---|
| Commit + push + PR body + PR comment | **2026-09-22 07:29:52 → 07:29:58 UTC** |

| Staleness gap | **~19 h 07 m** — all 5 `Next Move` items already done |
| Compactions in session | **5** (`seq 448, 731, 911, 1087, 1396`) |
| Prior summary (#4, `seq 1087`) | showed the task as correctly **Active** → never reconciled into #5 |
| False-state propagation | repeated at `seq 1511` (~**24 h** after completion) and written into a handoff file |
| Verified against | `git status` clean, `fork/main == 6042e3f`, PR comment API |

Differences from #28063 that I think matter:

1. **Trigger** — #28063 is manual `/compact`; this is **automatic** (`"reason": "auto"`), fires with no user action.
2. **Section labels** — #28063 targets `## Next Steps`; here the stale entries are in `## Work State → Active` and `## Next Move`. A fix scoped only to `Next Steps` would miss these.
3. **Downstream propagation** — the stale state reached a *later session*, which reported it to the user as fact. #28063 covers in-session repetition only.
